title: GitHub and the Fork-and-Pull Collaboration Model (2008)
explainer: GitHub launched in 2008, built on top of Git, and added a web-based social layer on top of it: forking a repository and submitting a pull request. That turned Git from a command-line tool for tracking versions into the default way strangers collaborate on code across the internet. Git itself has no built-in notion of a "pull request" - fork-and-pull is a workflow GitHub's founders designed on top of Git, which is why cloning a repo is a Git operation but opening a pull request is a GitHub (the website) operation.
